sanskrit_verse:
ṛṇे लेख्यं साक्षिणो वा युक्तिलेशादयो 'पि वा /
दैविकी वा क्रिया प्रोक्ता प्रजानां हितकाम्यया // BrhS_1,4.20
transliteration: ṛṇe lekhyaṃ sākṣiṇo vā yuktileśādayo 'pi vā / daivikī vā kriyā proktā prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā // BrhS_1,4.20
sph_interpretive_translation: In matters of debt, written records, witnesses, or even minimal evidence may be accepted; alternatively, divine action is declared effective when undertaken for the welfare of the people.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from alignment with the welfare of the populace
Evidence is valid in proportion to its capacity to restore integrity
Causation includes both empirical and divine dimensions
Responsibility arises from conscious intent towards collective well-being
Restoration logic prioritizes completion over judgment
executable_legal_axioms: IF a claim involves ṛṇa (debt) AND written documentation exists, THEN accept documentation as prima facie evidence.
IF no material evidence is present, BUT witness testimony aligns with dharmic sequence, THEN validate through sequential consciousness verification.
IF neither documents nor witnesses suffice, THEN invoke divine causality IF the act was performed for prajāhita (public welfare).
IF any evidence supports restoration of balance without punitive intent, THEN prioritize such evidence in adjudication.
IF all empirical means fail AND intent aligns with cosmic order, THEN recognize daivic kriyā as valid judicial input.
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes that while documentary and testimonial evidence remains primary, the court may also acknowledge acts of divine origin when performed with clear intention for public good. The threshold of responsibility lies not in fault alone, but in alignment with dharma and societal upliftment.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa here expands beyond sensory perception to include divine cognition when guided by hitakāmyatā. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures that actions unfold sequentially through lawful and spiritual causes. Responsibility is assigned based on capacity to sustain harmony rather than impose penalty. This reflects the non-punitive reality where justice serves evolution, not vengeance.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process by verifying existing agreements or debts through available lekhya or sākṣi
Engage yukti-based inquiry to reconstruct truth where data is incomplete
Invoke daivic validation protocol when action stems purely from desire for collective benefit
Realign debtor's consciousness through dharmic education and voluntary repayment facilitation
Ensure creditor's integrity is preserved via transparent reconciliation mechanisms
final_declaration: This law proceeds solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. It affirms that Dharma stands restored through recognition of evidence, divine will, and public welfare. There is no punishment—only alignment with Sanātana Nyāya, wherein consciousness itself becomes the ultimate judge.
